chosen.premise: Pidgeot can spot splashing Magikarp from 3,300 feet up, then dive-hunt at Mach 2.
chosen.hook: Pidgeot can find a Magikarp from 3,300 feet in the air.
chosen.visualIdea: A tiny Magikarp splash seen from a 3,300-foot altitude overlay, then Pidgeot locks on and streaks down at Mach 2.
chosen.note: A highly Pidgeot-specific hunting mechanic with a striking altitude-to-speed sequence. The entries support spotting Magikarp at 3,300 feet and Mach 2 flight, though they do not explicitly say the attack is a Mach 2 dive.

candidates.premise: Pidgeot combines Mach 2 flight with wings powerful enough to bend tall trees and talons feared as weapons.
candidates.hook: Pidgeot is a Mach 2 bird that can bend trees with its wings.
candidates.visualIdea: Three escalating stat-style reveals: Mach 2 flight, talon close-up, then a wingbeat forcing tall trees sideways.
candidates.note: Excellent power profile combining speed, talons, and tree-bending wings. It is well supported, but slightly broad and less focused than the altitude-based hunting premise.

candidates.premise: Pidgeot's gorgeous wings and head feathers attract trainers, but it spreads those same wings to intimidate enemies.
candidates.hook: Pidgeot's prettiest feature is also its threat display.
candidates.visualIdea: Split screen: trainers admire Pidgeot's glossy crest, then the wings snap open as an enemy recoils.
candidates.note: A clear, supported contradiction: the same beautiful plumage that attracts trainers helps intimidate enemies. Strong visual contrast, though less mechanically surprising than the hunting angle.

candidates.premise: Mega Pidgeot grows from 1.5 m and 39.5 kg to 2.2 m and 50.5 kg without changing its types.
candidates.hook: Mega Pidgeot gets 70 centimeters taller—and keeps both types.
candidates.visualIdea: A silhouette ruler shows Pidgeot rising from 1.5 m to 2.2 m while a scale climbs from 39.5 to 50.5 kg.
candidates.note: Precise, easy-to-visualize measurements with solid data support, but the size increase is more of a stat reveal than a surprising Pidgeot-specific story.

candidates.premise: Pidgeot needs only a few wing flaps to create a gusty windstorm—and full force can bend tall trees.
candidates.hook: How many flaps does it take for Pidgeot to make a windstorm?
candidates.visualIdea: Count three wing flaps as the gust escalates from swirling leaves to tall trees visibly bending.
candidates.note: The windstorm and tree-bending claims are well supported and visually strong, but 'a few' is imprecise and counting exactly three flaps would be invented.

candidates.premise: The #016 bird line keeps its Normal/Flying types through all three stages, ending with Pidgeot at Mach 2.
candidates.hook: Pidgey never changes type—but its final form flies at Mach 2.
candidates.visualIdea: Pidgey evolves at level 18, Pidgeotto evolves at level 36, then Pidgeot blasts through a Mach 2 speed gauge.
candidates.note: The unchanged typing and evolution milestones are accurate, but type continuity is not especially distinctive and the Mach 2 fact is not directly tied to the evolution itself.

rounds.request: No stronger angle is necessary; if refining it, avoid claiming an explicitly Mach 2 dive and frame the evidence as Pidgeot spotting Magikarp from 3,300 feet and flying at Mach 2.
